```
REVIEW: architect
VERDICT: approve
COMMENTS: Verified the central §2/§3 claim against source directly (working tree's src/driver.ts and src/envelope-detection.ts are byte-identical to origin/dev — `git diff origin/dev -- src/driver.ts src/envelope-detection.ts` is empty, so this is the real dev-branch code, not stale). Two-layer independence holds:

(1) Runtime-dispatch layer: driver.ts's only imports are `node:child_process`, `node:fs`, `node:crypto`, `node:os`, `node:path`, `yaml`, `./escalation-classification.ts`, `./envelope-detection.ts` — no plugin-hive/fork import anywhere. `resolveRuntimeRoute()` calls a Heimdall HTTP endpoint; `getAdapter()`/`ClaudeAdapter`/`OpencodeAdapter`/`CodexAdapter` (lines 313-591) are self-contained CLI-arg formatters with no fork-code overlap. Claim confirmed, not overstated.

(2) Question/envelope layer: `ForkedHiveDriver`'s own header (driver.ts:699-737) states it "drives the real headless-question-protocol shipped in firefly-events/plugin-hive#341"; envelope-detection.ts's header independently corroborates — "Full schema: hive/references/question-envelope-schema.md in plugin-hive-fork," flagged "LOAD-BEARING (confirmed via the epic's own spike + PR #341's review)." This is a direct client implementation, exactly as the document claims, not a parallel invention.

One nuance the document doesn't spell out but doesn't need to for its argument: the two layers aren't mutually isolated in the code — `ForkedHiveDriver.dispatchFresh()` (line 870) internally calls `resolveRuntimeRoute()`/`getAdapter()` from layer 1. That's fine (each layer's independence is evaluated against the *external* plugin-hive/fork dependency, not against each other), but worth a one-line clarification if this doc gets cited again.

AD-1 vs PR #341 distinction (§3) is coherent, not confused: `.pHive/CONTEXT.md` defines "Pantheon subprocess ABI" (line 26-29) exactly as cited — JSON-over-stdio `{method,params}`→`{result}`/`{error}`, AD-1 — and PR #341's file-based envelope format is genuinely one layer below it, used internally by `ForkedHiveDriver` to talk to the underlying CLI/skill rather than to Minerva's own external callers. Real architectural distinction, correctly grounded.

§4 risk framing checks out against the code: driver.ts:739-747 states production case is `MINERVA_HIVE_PLUGIN_DIR` unset, relying on marketplace-installed plugin-hive "(the production case, once PR #341 ships)"; setting the var is explicitly commented as a local-checkout testing stopgap. The "High" severity for #341 stalling is justified. One sharper feasibility wrinkle not explored in the doc: if `MINERVA_HIVE_PLUGIN_DIR` is unset today against a real marketplace plugin-hive that predates #341, `dispatchFresh()` doesn't error — the skill just runs without ever writing an envelope, and `surfaceNextQuestion()` (line 896) falls through to the `NO_PENDING_SENTINEL` "run may be complete" placeholder, silently indistinguishable from a legitimate completion. This is a silent-failure articulation of the same dependency the document already ranks as its top risk — worth a follow-up note, not a new escalation.

No architectural gaps found beyond what §4/§6/§7 already surface and prioritize correctly.
```
